hook: You wake up after eight hours and feel like you haven't slept. Here's the precise reason why.
topic: Sleep duration vs. sleep architecture — why hours aren't the right metric
body:
**You slept eight hours last night. And you still feel terrible. That's not a mystery — it's a measurement problem.**

Sleep isn't a single block of time. It's a sequence of four distinct stages that cycle roughly every 90 minutes across the night. Each stage does a different job. N2 consolidates memory. Slow-wave sleep clears metabolic waste from the brain. REM sleep restores emotional regulation and processes what happened during the day.

When your sleep is fragmented — by alcohol, by heat, by inconsistent timing — you're completing the cycles, but you're not spending enough time in the stages that actually restore you. You can clock eight hours and be structurally sleep-deprived at the same time.

The number of hours you sleep is not the metric that matters. The architecture inside those hours is.

So the next time you wake up exhausted after a full night, the question isn't "why didn't I sleep enough?" It's "which stage did I lose — and what disrupted it?"

Start there. I've linked a full breakdown in my bio.
